records.description: The Deutschlandstipendium supports high-achieving students at German universities with a monthly stipend of 300 euros, half financed by the Federal Government and half by private sponsors. It is income-independent, can be received in addition to BAföG, carries no social insurance contributions, and is granted for a minimum of two semesters and at most until the standard period of study has elapsed. Universities choose their own scholarship holders, so applications go through the university.

verification.notes: Verified on the official Deutschlandstipendium service page (English) on 10 October 2026: 300 euros per month (150 federal + 150 private), minimum two semesters and at most until the standard period of study has elapsed, income-independent with no BAföG offset, no social insurance contributions, and university-level selection with university-set deadlines.

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the Deutschlandstipendium): the application does not go to a national office - each participating university selects its own scholarship holders and sets its own deadline, so the practical first step is asking the international office or scholarship office at your German university for the current window. The award itself is modest but frictionless: 300 euros per month for at least two semesters and up to the end of the standard period of study, with no reduction of BAföG, no social insurance contributions to arrange and no application costs. Because the criteria are outstanding academic marks and prospective suitability for a future profession, prepare a short file that shows both sides - a strong transcript and a concrete argument for what your chosen field will enable you to do. As a first-year international student, ask specifically whether the university accepts applications from second or later semesters as well, since the official page does not publish one national rule and practice differs between institutions.

records.description: The DAAD study scholarship for Master's studies in all disciplines funds highly qualified international students from any country outside Germany for a full Master's degree programme at a German university. The scholarship pays 992 euros per month plus an annual lump sum of 460 euros for study, research and production costs, with travel allowance, DAAD-funded insurance and supplementary payments where applicable. Funding runs 10 to 24 months depending on the course length; tuition fees are not financed.

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the DAAD Master Studies all disciplines scholarship): this is the broad DAAD master's award, so if your plan is a full degree at a German university rather than a PhD grant, this is the entry point - it is not field-limited and includes English-taught programmes without a German-language requirement. The stipend is 992 euros per month plus an annual lump sum of 460 euros for study, research and production costs, and tuition is explicitly not financed, so combine it with the low-fee structure of German public universities when you pick the institution. Time the application to the official window: applications are possible between 1 June and the stated deadline, and the funding must begin in 2027, usually on 1 October 2027, so your file and language test (English or German around B1/B2 CEFR) need to be ready by early summer. The study plan with a time schedule and the second academic reference do a lot of work in the evaluation, so invest effort there rather than in a generic motivation letter.
